chunks: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! A man supplicates for a pregnant woman that God may make what is in her womb a well-formed male.'

He said: 'He may supplicate within the time between it and four months, for it is a sperm-drop for forty nights, a clot for forty nights, and a lump of flesh for forty nights — that completes four months.'

Then God sends two creative angels, and they say: 'O Lord! What shall we create — a male or a female, miserable or fortunate?' So that is told to them. Then they say: 'O Lord! What is its sustenance, what is its term, and what is its duration?' So that is told to them.

And its covenant is between its eyes — it gazes upon it. And it does not cease to be upright in the belly of its mother until, when its birth approaches, God Mighty and Majestic sends an angel to it. He rebukes it with a rebuke, so it comes out and forgets the covenant.

key_terms.خَلَّاقَيْن: Two creative/formative angels assigned to shape the embryo
key_terms.شَقِيّ / سَعِيد: Shaqi/Sa'id — the eternally wretched vs. the eternally fortunate; predestination terms
key_terms.عَلَقَة: 'Alaqa — the second stage: a blood clot or leech-like form
key_terms.مُضْغَة: Mudgha — the third stage: a lump of chewed flesh
key_terms.مِيثَاق: Mithaq — the primordial covenant; the soul's pledge before birth
key_terms.نُطْفَة: Nutfa — the initial stage: the sperm-drop or seminal fluid

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about embryonic development and the stages of human creation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) describes the stages of embryonic development — nutfa (sperm-drop), 'alaqa (clot), and mudgha (lump of flesh) — each lasting forty nights, completing four months. After this, two angels are sent to determine the child's sex, fortune, sustenance, and lifespan by divine decree. The narration also introduces the profound concept of the primordial covenant (mithaq), which the soul maintains in the womb but forgets upon birth — this is a foundational concept in Shia theology connecting to the covenant of Alast (Quran 7:172), representing humanity's pre-eternal acknowledgment of God's lordship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, or someone else who said, 
‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you! The man supplicates for the pregnancy that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> should Make whatever is in her belly to be a male, well-proportioned’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He can supplicate in what is between it and four months, for it is a seed for forty nights, and a clot for forty nights, and a lump for forty nights. So that completes four months.

Then Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sends two creating Angels, so they are both saying: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! What should we create, a male or a female, miserable or fortunate?’ So He<sup>azwj</sup> Says that. So they are both saying: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! What is its sustenance, and what is its term, and what is its duration?’ So He<sup>azwj</sup> Says that,

and its Covenant is between his eyes, and they look into it; and it does not cease to be vertical in the belly of its mother until when its exit approaches, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sends an Angel. So he rebukes it with a rebuke, so it comes out, and forgets the Covenant’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il or others who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, can a pregnant woman pray to Allah to make the child inside her a well formed boy?’
He (the Imam) said, ‘She can do so from conception up to the fourth month. Up to forty nights it is sperm, for another forty nights it is a clot and for another forty nights it is an embryo,

thereafter Allah sends two creative angles who ask, “O Lord, what must we create, a male or female, fortunate or unfortunate?” Their question is then answered. They then ask, “O Lord, what is his sustenance, when is the time of his death and what is the length of his life?” It all then is told to them

and his covenant is between his eyes to which he looks. He still is inside his mother until the time of his coming out draws near. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sends an angel who drives him out with reproach that sends him into shock and he forgets the covenant?”
